headline: Free Android app reveals Wi-Fi bottleneck, fixes network speed
summary: A simple app scan identified congested channels and recommended a switch, restoring optimal speeds without needing to reboot your router.
details: Slow internet speeds can be frustrating, especially when you have a high-speed connection. One user found that simply power-cycling their router no longer solved the issue, indicating a deeper problem.
The culprit was identified as Wi-Fi channel congestion. In densely populated areas, multiple networks operating on the same frequency can interfere with each other, creating a bottleneck.

A free Android app, WiFi Analyzer, was used to visualize network congestion. It identified that most neighboring networks were using the 2.4 GHz frequency on channels 36-50, while the user's network was on channel 48.

The app's 'Best Channels' section not only highlighted the overlapping signals but also recommended a less congested channel. Switching to this recommended channel resulted in 0% congestion and restored optimal Wi-Fi speeds.
While the app offers features like 'Who's Connected to WiFi' for a fee, alternatives like WiFiman can provide similar insights for free. Periodic channel checks can prevent future slowdowns.

If channel congestion isn't the issue, other factors like old router hardware or a single device hogging bandwidth could be the cause. Upgrading to a router with newer Wi-Fi standards and features, like a mesh router, is also recommended for persistent problems.

headline_marked: DeepSeek launches [[open-source agent harness]] to rival Claude Code
headline: DeepSeek launches open-source agent harness to rival Claude Code
summary: The AI lab also updates its V4-Pro model, but plans to significantly increase API pricing for developers.
details: DeepSeek is expanding its developer offerings with the launch of DeepSeek Harness v0.1, an open-source agent harness designed as an alternative to integrated coding environments like Anthropic's Claude Code. This move signifies DeepSeek's broader push into the developer tool space, aiming to provide more flexibility in how AI models are utilized for agentic workloads.

The new Harness, available under the MIT license, is built with a modular architecture allowing developers to swap out nearly every part of the agent runtime as plugins. This includes models, tools, skills, sessions, and more, offering a customizable framework for building complex AI agent systems.

Alongside the Harness, DeepSeek has released DeepSeek-V4-Pro, its updated flagship model. This model boasts native support for the OpenAI Responses API and integration with Codex, enhancing its capabilities for agentic tasks. The V4-Pro model is accessible via DeepSeek's web interface, mobile app, and API.

However, developers using DeepSeek's API will face substantially higher costs. The company is phasing out its existing flat API pricing for a new system with peak and off-peak rates, set to begin on August 16th. Even the discounted off-peak prices are expected to be significantly higher than current rates.

DeepSeek Harness enters developer preview with a warning of potential compatibility-breaking changes, indicating it's not yet a stable production platform. Despite this, its modular design positions DeepSeek to offer not just models but also the frameworks for assembling surrounding AI systems.

The open-source Harness can already perform essential agent functions such as inspecting repositories, editing files, executing shell commands, searching, planning, and invoking skills. These capabilities are key to differentiating it from simpler autocomplete systems and positioning it as a true coding agent.

DeepSeek's repository has already seen significant developer interest, with a notable number of GitHub stars and forks shortly after its launch, suggesting a strong initial reception for its open-source efforts.

While DeepSeek Harness offers a model-agnostic alternative to the infrastructure behind tools like Claude Code and Codex, it's important to note it's not yet a full replacement for the broader developer experience offered by those established products.
